content.text: Inflam of the pericardium, the outer layer of the ♡
(worse when supine & improved w/ sitting forward)
•pain may radiate to back, shoulder, neck, arm, or epigastric area
: best heard @ end expiration while upright & leaning forward
ST elevations in the precordial leads w/ assoc PR depressions in those leads
b/c they can interfere w/ myocard scar form
Accum of fluid in the pericardial space
Normally, about 5-15ml of fluid = in the pericardial space
: viral, idiopathic, immune, malig – lung CA MC, breast second MC, aortic dissection, uremia, prior chest radiation
: test of choice – ↑fluid in pericardial space
Pericardial effusion causing sig P on the ♡, impeding ♡ filling, leading to ↓CO & shock
: comp of acute pericarditis or trauma; malig MC ⍉traumatic cause
▪︎⍉confuse w/ tension PTX: hypotension + JVD + absent breath sounds
: exaggerated (>10mmHg) ↓ in systol P w/ inspiration
Dyspnea, fatigue, periph edema, shock, reflex tachy, cool extremities
(RV wall collapse in diastole; paradoxic septal motion in systole)
- vol resuscitation & pressor support if needed
Loss of pericardial elasticity (thickening, fibrosis, calcification) leading to
: fibrosis limits ventricular filling, ↓stroke vol & CO
(the lack of an inspir decline or an ↑ in jugular v. P w/ inspiration)
: ↑pitched diastol sound similar to S3 (sudden cessation of ventricular filling)
: pericardial calcification may be seen esp. on lat view, clear lung fields
– early diastol dip followed by a plateau if diastasis
for Sx relief as well as reduction of edema & venous P
